correctness.rationale: Fresh conditional Gaussian isotropy yields independent residual/captured chi-square norms and their beta ratio. The conditional first-passage hazard depends only on the dimension. Chernoff optimization gives exp[-(br/2)D(u||tau)] with the correct entropy orientation. Stirling plus one-sided beta-density Laplace asymptotics, uniformly over bounded positive moderate-deviation parameters, yield the stated lower-tail coefficient. Convexity bounds all earlier looks by a geometric tail, while a window of Theta(sqrt(r log r)) independent conditional opportunities has divergent integrated hazard on the other side of the threshold. Together these prove the precise limiting constant. The actual flat-spectrum squared projection error is exactly (r-k)/r, so premature acceptance is a genuine violation. The included verify.py passed 35,531 finite exact/numerical assertions including adaptive QR runs, but only the written argument proves the limit. All endpoint and rank-divisibility assumptions are explicitly specified.

value.rationale: The practical mathematical question is whether repeated independent Gaussian looks, each justified by an unbiased Frobenius estimate, preserve an algorithmic relative-error stopping guarantee. The exact finite failure law answers this without a heuristic independence assumption on the adaptive basis, and the nontrivial sharp sqrt(r log r) deficit quantifies how sequential risk accumulates at the constant-batch width used for fast matrix-free sampling. It separates algorithmic stopping and true approximation tolerance, provides a calibration benchmark and identifies which alterations require new analysis. Fixed flat spectrum is a natural worst-case degeneracy for low-rank range finding, not an arbitrary collection of parameters; the result is not claimed for actual complete HSS implementations.
